profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne campus sits in Loudoun County, Virginia, in and around Sterling, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn area data center corridor. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, went public in 2013, and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling VA (NVA4) publishes 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet in Loudoun County. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this represents roughly 275 racks. The campus sits in the Northern Virginia Ashburn corridor, a region with established data center infrastructure and grid connections serving the East Coast.

Sterling NVA4 ranks 20th among Virginia's 23 facilities with published capacity figures, holding 0.8 percent of the state's 1,375 MW total. Virginia's mapped inventory includes 326 data center sites, but only 23 have published specifications, so the state's actual capacity is substantially larger than the disclosed figure. The campus is one of many in a concentrated region, not an outlier.

The operator published no building-specific certifications and did not disclose total campus capacity, only this one facility's IT load. The published 11 MW figure provides no information about whether this campus can or will host large-scale AI training clusters. Without disclosed power density, cooling specifications, or water or grid capabilities, the campus cannot be assessed as a meaningful constraint or enabler of AI scaling.
